_comment: What each animation's blow does, in time and in space.
contact - the first tick the edge is dangerous.
through - how many ticks it stays dangerous.
cancel  - the earliest tick another blow may begin; not the end of the film.
reach   - how far in front of herself the edge gets, in blocks, at contact.
blade   - how far a weapon carries on past the hand. An input to reach, not
read by the game: it is written down so the arithmetic can be
checked by re-running the measurement.
checked - somebody has looked at the frames, rather than only measured them.
Look with tools/shape-look:
.\frames.ps1 <animation> out.png 1 side    the picture
.\reach.ps1                                every reach against every contact
.\reach.ps1 <animation>                    one of them, tick by tick
reach is measured off the animation, along the arm's own axis, exactly the
line the contact sheet draws. It is measured rather than chosen because it
was not: the fighting used to ask ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE, which is three
blocks and is a number about clicking on a mob with a mouse. So two people
punched each other from three and a half blocks apart.
The fist and the edge are different lines. On a horizontal swing the fist is
beside the body at the moment the edge crosses in front, so a hand plus a
blade is not a reach - the weapon has to be measured where it actually is.
